en: Exiled in Dapitan, national hero Jose Rizal sculpted a famous monument titled The Triumph of Science over Death.
The majestic Philippine eagle, our national bird, lays only one egg per breeding season.
The 1899 Malolos Constitution was the first democratic constitution ever established in Asia.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the two-way video telephone decades before modern video calls existed.
T'boli women in South Cotabato weave intricate T'nalak cloth using patterns revealed to them in dreams.
Before the Spanish arrived, ancient Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using their own script called Baybayin.
The Aklan Ati-Atihan festival inspired other major Philippine festivals by having participants paint their faces with black soot.
The tradition of Bayanihan literally began when neighbors carried an entire nipa hut on bamboo poles to a new location.
By law, the Philippine national flag must be flown upside down with the red stripe on top during times of war.
Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his massive Spoliarium painting.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people, would stretch halfway around the globe if laid end to end.
The Sangguniang Kabataan gives Filipino youth aged fifteen to seventeen an official voice in local village governance.
